_comment: Hand-authored. The halves of the two split pointer tables that no reader-bounded scan can claim.

regions.name: Object dispatch, low bytes (types 1-126)
regions.description: The low half of bank 6's split object-behaviour table: $821E does LDA $815D,Y / PHA / LDA $80DE,Y / PHA / RTS with Y = type AND $7F. Type 0 is filtered by BEQ at $8213, so $80DE - low[0] - is never read, and it is in fact the last byte of the traced code before it (the same overlap the metasprite table uses). Types 1-126 are here; type 127's low byte is $815D, the first byte of the high half, which is never read as high[0]. So this is 126 bytes between code and the high half. CORRECTION: CLAUDE.md said find-tables.py claimed both halves; it only ever claimed $815D - a reader-bounded table cannot bound the half that no later read follows.

regions.name: Metasprite pointers, high bytes
regions.description: The high half of the split metasprite table: $CC3C LDA $C319,Y with Y = the object's $0548 id. 141 entries, ending exactly where the first metasprite record begins at $C3A6 - the structural bound; no later read bounds it, which is why tools/find-tables.py claimed only the low half at $C28D. Its first byte is also low[140]; high[0] is never read because id 0 is filtered by BEQ $CC44. CORRECTION: CLAUDE.md described both halves as claimed; this one was not.
